newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil down on correction, Iraqi return.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil down on correction, Iraqi return.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil closed weaker on Monday on technical correction after Friday's new five-year record trade and news of the resumption of Iraqi crude exports on Tuesday, traders said.
Physical gas oil was offered down to a low of $34.00 a barrel free-on-board Singapore, 45 cents lower than Friday's traded record level, but no buying interest emerged.

Similarly weaker sentiment were also seen in the swaps market with January gas oil traded down to a low of $32.37 a barrel from an intra-day high of $32.75, well off Friday's traded high of $33.07, brokers said.
The declining prices came despite news of an unexpected partial shutdown of a thermal cracker at the Shell Singapore refinery over the weekend which led to a 5,000 tonne per day product loss.

Sentiment was still bullish due to firm Chinese buying amid critical low stocks and pre-Lunar New Year demand. On Friday, a record $262 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to south China was paid for a 25,000-tonne cargo for delivery late-December.
The January jet fuel/gas oil spread fell by 20 cents from Friday to $1.50/$1.70. Traders said the fall was due to gas oil's slide while jet was bullish on North Asia winter demand.

The naphtha/gasoline spread was under pressure due to strong demand for naphtha which pushed prices nearly on par with gasoline. Gasoline was traded at $26.20 per barrel, down just 5 cents from Friday's deal. Singapore January naphtha swaps traded at $25.10 and $25.20 a barrel, up from $24.65/$24.90 on Friday.

One trader said demand for second-half January was strong with one cargo sought by Thailand while Japan endusers have yet to emerge. A South Korean petrochemical company won the December Indian low aromatic naphtha tender at $14.87 a tonne below Japanese quotes fob Vizag which translates to $5 over Japanese prices, c-and-f North Asia.
